doc.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024

chapter: Playing, recording and making a living
title: Feeling the clave and swing
summary: Rowe describes struggling to hear the clave; she says it can be felt, and Cuban music came more quickly to her than swing pocket.

bands.name: Alex Torres and the Latin Kings

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah. Years ago when I was booking groups for school shows we had a group come from Albany, Alex Torres and the Latin Kings. It was wonderful. And I got aggravated with myself because there was some times I couldn’t find one.
And they go, “Just listen to the clave.” And I’m watching and I go wait — no one’s playing the clave specifically.
It’s still a bit of a mystery to me but it’s so — as Shaughnessy said, “It’s so infectious after a while” he says, “I don’t know where one is but it sure feels good.” So.
That’s so true, it really is. Yeah. Sometimes you can’t — you can feel it, and your body feels it, if something like goes off, right? It’s like having two left shoes on or something like that.
Just this morning I was listening to one of your videos and I couldn’t really find where one was but I all of a sudden noticed that my foot was tapping, so, very unconsciously.
I’m not sure what the conclusion is there but.

It does take time, you know. Cuban music came more quickly to me than Larry in terms of the clave and stuff. But for me, when Larry plays a beautiful feeling of swing and sometimes I don’t feel as comfortable, you know, as he is with finding the pocket in music that is more, you know, in the pocket swing. It’s something that you have to spend a lot of time with and work on.
